question.text: During DD, an AIF discloses that its fund administrator is a related party of the investment manager. From a Series XIX-A governance perspective, this raises concerns about:

answer.text: Cost efficiency, as related party services may be cheaper
Fund governance and segregation of functions, service-provider independence and conflict checks, related-party/affiliate disclosure, and the integrity of fund accounting and valuation reporting
Nothing, as related party arrangements are always beneficial

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook treats administrators and other service providers as part of fund governance and emphasises segregation of functions, absence of conflicts, service-provider conflict checks, related-party/affiliate disclosure, and the cost and integrity of fund accounting and valuation reporting. It also restricts related-party arrangements for custodians. A related-party administrator therefore touches every one of these governance prompts. The Trap: Possible cost savings do not offset weakened independent oversight, and related-party arrangements are not inherently beneficial. Note: Keyed option was rewritten around source-backed fund governance, segregation of functions, service-provider independence/conflict checks, related-party disclosure, and fund accounting/valuation reporting. The administrator-specific "independent NAV / record-keeping / independent-auditor compensating control" wording was removed, along with the Cross-Exam and Pro-Tip paragraphs.
